the energy-minimization method for finite-difference calculations is a fast and accurate alternative to time integration of the LLG equation, and that the method is especially useful when computing hysteresis curves.

the development of efficient numerical methods for the micromagnetic simulation of large-scale systems.
the development of an energy-minimization algorithm that is suitable to solve hysteresis problems in finite-difference magnetostatics.
the development of a highly efficient energy-minimization code for finite-difference simulations of magnetic systems, which is capable of computing large hysteresis cycles with high precision.

we present a new efficient method that can be used in micromagnetic simulations to calculate hysteresis curves of large systems with an accuracy that is comparable to the solution of Landau-Lifschitz-Gilbert equations.
the presented energy-minimization algorithm allows to calculate accurate hystereses with a reasonable computational cost.

energy-minimization algorithms can be used to speed up hysteresic computations in micromagnetics.
the energy-minimization approach is a viable and efficient alternative to time integration for the computation of the hysteresis loop of large magnetic systems.
